title: FIG. 03 · The loop, closed
summary: The homepage's one pinned scroll: it opens on the loop most teams run (capital in, campaigns run, knowledge lost at a red ✕, a dashed reset that carries nothing back) and, frame by frame, lands Narrative Systems, GTM Infrastructure and GTM Intelligence onto that same loop until the dashed reset is redrawn as a solid red return and the count carried forward climbs from 00 to 04.
story: It turns the letter's 'every quarter starts from zero' into a drawing the reader recognises as his own, builds the three layers into it until the loop closes, and hands the principle a system whose output is one clear signal: Compounding pipeline exits right, just before 'In a noisy market, the clearest company wins.'
motion: On the homepage the section holds the screen for 1600px of scrolling while five frames play one at a time; a thin five-step rail above the text shows where you are. Scrolling back up reverses everything.

Frame 0 (the loop most teams run) moves with your scroll: a dot runs down Capital in → Campaigns run → Knowledge lost three times and falls out at the red ✕ each time. The dashed Reset carries nothing; Carried forward stays at 00 and ERR · Q1 = Q9 stays on.

Frames 1–3 play once as you reach them: each layer drops onto its point on the loop (0.7s) and the loop's words give way to the layer's name, then its own drawing settles. Narrative: five jittery lines calm into straight text rules. Infrastructure: a three-point route draws across the plate. Intelligence: an open ring closes and the red ✕ dissolves into it.

Frame 4 (the return) moves with your scroll: the error stamp clears, numerals 01 02 03 appear, and a dot leaves Intelligence drawing the dashed Reset solid red behind it, in the same place, back up to Narrative. Then three more laps. Each pass through Intelligence lays down a ring; each arrival back at Narrative steps Carried forward 01 → 04. Reroute effort branches into Infrastructure, the plates settle closer together (56 → 32px gaps), and Compounding pipeline exits bottom right.
After the pin the loop rests closed and still: no looping dot (the method section owns the page's one ambient loop). Then the quiet door, 'Find your weakest layer', appears below.
Entrance (homepage): as the section comes into view the hairline draws, the label, two-line statement, red rule and caption rise, and the loop's spine draws top to bottom.

This review page is a still contact sheet: the section's head, then the five frames, drawn by the same code at fixed points. It only reveals once (the head rises, the frames fade in one after another); it never plays the frames. Review the real scroll on the stitched homepage.

Reduced motion, and phones: no pin. The broken loop and its caption, then the three layers as a plain list, then the closed loop (four rings, red return, Carried forward · 04) with the return text. On phones the two drawings re-set their labels for the small size, so they stay readable (12px at 390 wide) instead of shrinking with the drawing.
addressed: Stack and architecture were approved but sat as twins and disagreed on the count (four layers against three). They are now one drawing with three layers, built into one loop.

Your statechange note ('looks like an afterthought… same layout as the previous section… tell a story'): stop-resetting and start-compounding are now the first and last frames of the same drawing, with the same counter going from 00 to 04, in the page's most-watched spot rather than a separate plate.

'Understandable at first glance': frame 0 is the familiar broken loop (a red ✕ at Knowledge lost, a dashed Reset, Carried forward · 00); the last frame is the same loop with the reset drawn solid red, four rings deposited and 04 carried forward. No adjective is needed.
Layout repetition: there is no plate, caption band or toggle here. It is the page's only pinned scroll, showing one frame at a time beside its own text, which no other section does.
Each layer arrives with its own movement (noise settling, a route drawing, a ring closing), so frames 1–3 are not three identical drops.
The story says it, never claims it: 'Three layers. One closed loop.' is shown, not argued, and the quiet door below ('If we're not the fix, the audit says so') keeps the ask honest.
notes: Built as one drawing function used three ways: the homepage pin, the reduced-motion/phone stack, and this contact sheet. Every frame on the sheet is the real drawing at a fixed point. PIN: per the round-3 override it is not a ScrollTrigger pin (that breaks under the prototype's page zoom). The section is a tall track (screen height + 1600px) with a sticky stage; progress is measured from the track's position on scroll and resize, smoothed over 0.6s like a scrub. Thresholds follow STORY: 280 / 560 / 840 / 1120 of 1600px. Tested at 1440×900 (zoom 1) and 1280×800 (zoom 0.889): the stage fills the screen, the frame stays centred, all five frames step, and scrolling back reverses them. The stage scales the frame down on screens shorter than about 730px. CONTACT SHEET: the frames are shown at half size, so their labels are re-set for that size (about 14px on screen, the same as in the pin) rather than shrunk to 7px. At that size the ERR · Q1 = Q9 stamp moves from beside the Reset line into each frame's caption row, the two long labels (Reroute effort, Compounding pipeline) break onto two lines, and the One cycle · one quarter dimension is left out (it is the return's subtitle). The same compact labels serve phones. The sheet opens on the section's real head (label + Three layers. / One closed loop.) so the type can be judged here; the one sentence beside it is review copy, not homepage copy. ENTRANCE (homepage): the section plays its own entrance when the stage is about a fifth of the way into view, because the shared player waits until 22% of this very tall section is visible (about 600px in), which would flash the content. Entrance hooks retire once played, so a resize or a full-page capture cannot replay them. FULL-PAGE CAPTURES: a still capture of the whole homepage shows about 1600px of empty graphite above the resting final frame. That is the scroll distance the pin consumes; live, the stage always fills the screen. See the per-frame captures system-S-pin-0…4. Copy is verbatim from the approved stack, architecture and nav, and from the About page's origin telemetry and closing panel ('the readout' adapted to 'the audit' per STORY). 'Compounding pipeline' is this section's one use of the word. Red appears in one place at a time on the homepage: the ✕ in frames 0–2, dissolving in frame 3, then the return in frame 4 (plus the label square and the 48×2 rule). The contact sheet necessarily shows several frames' reds side by side.
